I've been working this same 2 mu for most of my life. Chili is what I know, and the market has been decent enough to keep at it. My son works in the city now, so it's just me and my wife managing the farm. 2 mu of chili is about right for the two of us to handle, especially during harvest when it gets heavy.

I'm going to plant hybrid seed this year. I switched away from traditional seed about ten years ago and the yields are noticeably better. Costs more up front, but on only 2 mu I can afford the better seed. The hybrid varieties also hold up better against anthracnose, which hit us badly a few years back.

For fertilizer, I'll put down base fertilizer before transplanting — mostly phosphorus and potassium to get roots established — then top-dress with urea during the vegetative and early fruiting stages. I know I use a bit more nitrogen than the extension station says, but chili on my plot responds well to it and I've never had burning problems.

I'll irrigate from the well. Chili doesn't like drought stress when it's flowering or setting fruit, so I irrigate more frequently than some crops. I count on about 10 waterings through the season — less in wet years, I adjust as I go.

Pests are the main worry. Aphids, spider mites, and anthracnose. I spray on a calendar basis mostly, with extra applications if I see pressure. Seven or eight times is typical for me.

I use rotary tillage in spring before transplanting. It breaks up the soil nicely and I've done it this way for decades.
